subject: Dedicated GPU reservation: priority matrix & ops timeline
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Ward <elliot@horizon-labs.com>; Alex Johnson <alex@horizon-labs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU reservation: priority matrix & ops timeline

Hi Elliot / Alex —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we all have the same action plan. I kept this intentionally short.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production tail latency spikes during peak training/eval windows causing customer-facing inference timeouts (p95 occasionally hitting 480–600ms).
- Regulatory requirement to isolate PHI-related model serving (can’t mix with other tenants).
- Need predictable monthly spend for Q1 planning and procurement sign-off.

Goals we discussed:
- Provision a reserved, isolated GPU pool for the Horizon inference workload with predictable SLOs (target p95 <120ms for 4k token requests).
- Preserve burst capacity for unexpected traffic with defined cost/usage policy.
- Provide audit logs and key rotation that satisfy Horizon’s compliance team.

Redwood proposed reservation (initial):
- Size: 8 x A100 equivalent GPUs (reserved pool, single-tenant silo).
- Isolation: Tenant-level pool with network isolation + private KMS integration.
- Throughput expectation: ~200 qps sustained (~1M tokens/hour) with autoscale buffer for short bursts.
- SLA ask: 99.9% availability for serving runtime; escalation path with 15m paging for Sev1.

Attachments: I’m attaching a draft SOW and a capacity_estimate workbook that maps expected qps to slot sizing.

Mutual action items (owners + target dates):
1) Redwood: Finalize SOW + pricing proposal (Stephanie) — target 2026-10-28.
2) Horizon: Confirm procurement contact + preferred billing term (Alex / Procurement) — target 2026-10-27.
3) Tech deep-dive with infra (Redwood Ops + Horizon infra) — schedule for week of Oct 26; suggested 60m.
4) Security questionnaire (Horizon to send out any remaining items; Redwood to respond within 3 business days).

Questions for you before we lock the SOW:
- Is 8 GPUs in the right ballpark for your peak? If you expect higher peaks we can propose a burst pool + overage caps.
- Any constraints on contract term (12 vs 24 months) or invoicing cadence?

Thanks — I’ll push an updated SOW by EOD Wednesday assuming no major scope changes.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie —

Appreciate the crisp recap. This matches our internal notes very closely. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- 8 GPUs is a reasonable starting point given our current traffic; we’ll validate with internal telemetry this week and revert if we think we need +2.
- Procurement prefers 12 month term but will consider 24 month for a modest discount — I’ll loop Procurement in on Monday with the SOW.
- Burst: yes, please include a burst policy in the SOW (we need a clear overage rate and a pre-approved burst credit threshold).
- Security: our compliance lead will send a short SOC2 + encryption Q on Monday; audit logs and KMS integration are must-haves.

Procurement contact: Procurement <procurement@horizon-labs.com> (cc’d)

We’re good to schedule the infra deep-dive. Can Redwood do Tue Oct 27 10:00–11:00 PT? If not, we can do Wed.

Thanks — Elliot

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Horizon - reservation asks + procurement timeline

Folks — forwarding the thread with Horizon. High priority: procurement and compliance asks up front, and they want an infra deep-dive early next week. Key items for ops/engineering below — please review and add any risk/requirements inline.

=== TL;DR required by Ops ===
- Reserved pool: 8 A100-eq, tenant-silo, private KMS, 99.9% serving SLA.
- Burst policy: pre-approved credit up to 30% sustained for 10 minutes; overage billing at negotiated rate.
- Compliance: SOC2 + audit logs export to S3 (retention 1 year) + key rotation every 90 days.

Priority matrix (please confirm feasibility / blockers):
1) Tenant isolation model (network and runtime-level separation) — blocker? expected change to infra?
2) KMS integration (customer-managed keys) — Feasibility + estimate for engineering effort.
3) Burst pool implementation — can we use existing burst slots? How do we enforce pre-approved credit and stopgap policy?
4) SLA/uptime & on-call escalation — confirm our 15m paging for Sev1 and contractual language we can accept.

Immediate asks:
- Ben: can you provide a short ops runbook snippet (1 page) for onboarding a reserved silo? Needed for SOW.
- Rishi: engineering estimate for KMS integration and log export (rough hours and earliest delivery date).

I’ll coordinate the Tue/Wed deep-dive if Ops/Eng can make Tue 10–11 PT — Horizon specifically requested that slot.

Thanks — steph

Subject: Re: Fwd: Horizon - reservation asks + procurement timeline

Steph —

Thanks for the heads-up and forwarding. Quick responses inline to your priority matrix:

1) Tenant isolation model — feasible. We already support silo pools; ops checklist is ~6 items (network ACL, dedicated GPU nodes, tenant RBAC, logging pipeline, kms binding, monitoring). No infra changes required, just provisioning.

2) KMS integration — doable but non-trivial. Rough engineering estimate: 3–5 full-time days to wire customer-managed keys for a single account, plus QA (1 day). We need access to their KMS test credentials and an acceptance criteria doc from their security team.

3) Burst pool — can be implemented with existing burst slots and token-based enforcement. To meet their pre-approved credit ask we’ll implement a soft cap plus automated throttling and a billing meter. Ops effort: configuration + test ~2 days. Policy/legal needs to sign off on overage language; can Steph include suggested wording in SOW?

4) SLA / escalation — 15m page for Sev1 is on the table. Legal will want standard force majeure & maintenance windows; I recommend keeping 99.9% availability and a 2x service credit cap for downtime.

Deliverables I’ll have by Tue EOD if you confirm the Tue 10–11 PT deep-dive:
- One-page onboarding runbook (PDF stub)
- Burst policy draft language (text)
- Ops acceptance checklist for tenant silo

Rishi — can you confirm the KMS work estimate and any blocking dependencies? If we get test creds by Tue morning, we can demonstrate a POC in the week following the contract signature.

Ben
Director, Customer Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
